results.label: evicted-single
results.prompt: How do I list all evicted pods?

message.content:
To list all evicted pods across all namespaces, you can use the following `kubectl` command:

```sh
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.reason == "Evicted")'
```

This command filters the JSON output of `kubectl get pods -A` to show only those pods where the `status.reason` is "Evicted".

If you want to list evicted pods in a specific namespace, replace `-A` with `-n <namespace>`:

```sh
kubectl get pods -n <namespace> -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.status.reason == "Evicted")'
```

Replace `<namespace>` with the actual namespace name.

results.label: concurrent-rollout
results.prompt: How do I check deployment rollout status and view logs in namespace demo? Include oc and kubectl examples.

message.content:
To check the rollout status of a deployment and view logs in the `demo` namespace, you can use the following commands:

### Deployment Rollout Status
To check the rollout status of a deployment, you can use the `kubectl rollout status` command. This command will wait until the deployment is fully rolled out.

```sh
kubectl rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```

Replace `<deployment-name>` with the actual name of your deployment.

### Logs of Pods
To view logs of the Pods managed by a deployment, you can use the `kubectl logs` command. This command will show the logs of the current Pods.

```sh
kubectl logs -l app=<app-label> -n demo
```

Replace `<app-label>` with the label that identifies your application.

### Using `oc` Commands
If you are using `oc` (OpenShift client), the commands are similar:

#### Deployment Rollout Status
```sh
oc rollout status deployment/<deployment-name> -n demo
```

#### Logs of Pods
```sh
oc logs -l app=<app-label> -n demo
```

### Prerequisites
- Ensure you have `kubectl` or `oc` installed and configured to access your OpenShift or Kubernetes cluster.
- Ensure you have the necessary permissions to view deployments and logs in the `demo` namespace.

### Notes
- The `kubectl rollout status` command will only show the status of the deployment itself, not the individual Pods.
- The `kubectl logs` command will show the logs of the current Pods, which may change over time as the deployment rolls out new Pods.
- If you need to view logs of a specific Pod, you can use the `kubectl logs <pod-name>` command, but you need to know the name of the Pod.
